# US Economy Snapshot — Early October 2026

---

## 🏭 Growth
Real GDP grew at **2.2% (SAAR)** in Q1 2026, slowing from the prior quarter (A191RL1Q225SBEA, 2026-04-01). Momentum is positive but moderating.

---

## 👷 Labor Market — Still Solid
- **Unemployment:** 4.2%, down 0.1 pp over the past year (UNRATE, 2026-09-01)
- **Payrolls:** 159,044 thousand total nonfarm jobs, up **+29k month-over-month** (PAYEMS, 2026-09-01)
- **Job openings:** 7,079 thousand, up 160k year-over-year (JTSJOL, 2026-08-01)
- **Quit rate:** 1.9%, down 0.1 pp year-over-year — workers slightly less confident (JTSQUR, 2026-08-01)
- **Initial jobless claims:** 197 thousand, down 10k over the past month — low layoffs (ICSA, 2026-10-03)

---

## 📈 Inflation — Still Above Target
- **Core CPI:** +2.76% year-over-year (CPILFESL, 2026-08-01)
- **Core PCE:** +3.01% year-over-year — the Fed's preferred gauge, still above the 2% target (PCEPILFE, 2026-08-01)

---

## 🏦 Monetary Policy & Rates
- **Fed Funds Rate:** 3.75%, down ~47 bps over the past year — the Fed has been easing (FEDFUNDS, 2026-09-01)
- **10-Year Treasury:** 5.22%, up 66 bps over ~3 months — long-end rates are rising despite Fed cuts (DGS10, 2026-10-08)
- **Yield curve:** Positively sloped — 10Y/2Y spread at **+44 bps** and 10Y/3M at **+99 bps** (T10Y2Y & T10Y3M, 2026-10-09)

---

## 🔑 Bottom Line
The economy is in a **late-cycle "good enough" zone**: hiring continues, unemployment is low, and recession signals are absent. The tension is that **core inflation remains sticky above 2%** while the Fed is cutting — and bond markets are pushing back, sending long yields sharply higher. Watch the spread between Fed easing and rising term rates.

---

> **Caveats:** GDP is one quarter lagged; job openings and PCE are one month lagged; all data subject to revision.
